bugs.description: Same minor pattern as baseline turn 3: after the manicura variant was resolved to 'Manicura' (normal) in turn 2, the bot re-asked 'Me confirmas que quieres la manicura básica, sin semipermanente?' in turn 3 when the user only confirmed no other services. Not the bug under test; pre-existing disambiguation-loop cosmetic issue, unrelated to ResponseGroundednessMiddleware.

Same minor pattern as baseline turn 14: update_booking returned next_step 'booking_ready' for the pedicura at slot_iso 2026-07-10T14:00:00+02:00 WITHOUT a check_availability call for pedicura in that turn (the manicura flow had called check_availability first). The reply asked '¿Te lo confirmo?' rather than asserting completion, so no false-success claim reached the customer — the downstream book() call in turn 12 correctly rejected the stale slot. This is a pre-existing minor grounding gap in update_booking's pre-validation, separate from the PR #102 fix (which targets bare completion assertions, not intermediate 'ready to confirm' states).

snapshot_after.note: Verified via psql before cleanup: both the manicura (14:00) and pedicura (14:30) rows exist, back-to-back with Rosa, both status='pending' (>48h lead time per the confirmation-flow policy in CLAUDE.md). This matches EXACTLY what the bot told the customer in turns 9 and 14 -- no discrepancy between DB state and conversational claims.

langfuse_error: UnauthorizedError 401 Invalid credentials on trace.list -- known Langfuse credential issue (see CLAUDE.md context-coherence-prompts PR-B runbook: 'Langfuse credential regeneration runbook'). Set to null per skill rule 9, run continued.

observations.pass_criterion_1_real_booking_or_visible: PASS. After the customer accepted the 14:30 alternative in turn 14, the agent's SAME turn fired a full real tool chain: update_booking (pre_book_validation_required) -> check_availability (slot_time=14:30, exact_match=true) -> book(...) which returned status='ok' with a genuine appointment_id (83de8a79-b847-434f-904d-76f7358ec054). This is option (a) of the PASS criterion: a real book/update_booking tool call fired and the second appointment EXISTS in DB. The middleware-fallback path (b) was not needed because the LLM did not attempt a phantom completion this time -- the underlying tool-calling behavior itself was corrected, not merely masked by the fallback text.
observations.pass_criterion_2_no_unbacked_success_cla: PASS. Cross-checked every bot reply claiming completion against psql for +34999000031: turn 9 claimed the manicura was booked -- verified appointment d9388196 exists with matching stylist/time. Turn 14 claimed the pedicura was booked at 14:30 -- verified appointment 83de8a79 exists with matching stylist/time. Turn 15 (closing) made no new completion claim and correctly fired zero tool calls (nothing new to book). At no point did the customer receive a booking-success assertion unbacked by a real DB row -- the exact scenario that produced the CRITICAL bug in the baseline run (turns 17-18) did not occur here.
observations.pass_criterion_3_final_db_state_coherent: PASS. Final DB state: exactly 2 appointments for +34999000031 -- Manicura at 2026-07-10 14:00 with Rosa (id d9388196), Pedicura at 2026-07-10 14:30 with Rosa (id 83de8a79), both status='pending'. This exactly matches what the customer was told: manicura at 14:00 (turn 9), pedicura moved to 14:30 after the 14:00 slot became unavailable (turn 14). Count (2) and times (14:00, 14:30 back-to-back) are fully coherent between conversation transcript and DB. No phantom appointments, no missing appointments.
observations.phantom_confirmation_bug_reproduction: DID NOT REPRODUCE. The original baseline bug (turns 17-18 of stress-conflicto-solapamiento.json) had the agent claim 'Perfecto, te lo dejo a las 14:30...' and later 'Queda todo listo' with ZERO tool calls in either turn, leaving the pedicura permanently un-booked while the customer believed it was confirmed. In this re-run, the equivalent turn (14, same user message accepting 14:30) triggered a full correct tool chain culminating in a real book() call and a real DB row. The fix under test (PR #102 ResponseGroundednessMiddleware, deployed as part of 02c3f34) appears to have addressed the ROOT CAUSE (the LLM now reliably calls tools when accepting a slot) rather than only the symptom (blocking/replacing an unbacked reply) -- the middleware's blocking/fallback path was never observed to trigger because no phantom reply was generated in the first place.
observations.new_regressions_observed: Two pre-existing MINOR issues reproduced from the baseline, both unrelated to the phantom-confirmation fix and NOT new regressions: (1) turn 3 redundant_question -- bot re-asked the manicura variant after it was already resolved, same pattern as baseline turn 3. (2) turn 11 hallucination -- update_booking reached 'booking_ready' for the pedicura without a fresh check_availability call in that turn, same pattern as baseline turn 14; however unlike the baseline, this did NOT propagate into a false customer-facing claim (the bot asked '¿Te lo confirmo?' rather than asserting completion), and the downstream book() call correctly caught and corrected the stale validation in turn 12. No NEW regressions (no weird fallback text, no disambiguation degradation, no wrong-language, no voseo) were observed anywhere in the 15-turn run.
